what: Coherent makes lasers, optical transceivers and the engineered materials behind them. Data centre optics for AI networks have become its fastest-growing business, alongside industrial lasers and telecom components.
customers: Cloud and AI data centre operators, network equipment makers, industrial manufacturers, carmakers and semiconductor firms.
money: optical transceivers and components for networks
lasers for cutting, welding and semiconductor processing
moat: Vertical integration from the crystal and the laser chip up to the finished module, which few optical companies can match.
risks: Debt of about $4 billion from the II-VI and Coherent merger
Optical transceiver prices fall as volumes rise
Revenue is concentrated in a few very large cloud customers
Return on invested capital of about 5% is still low after the merger
opportunities: Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
AI networks need faster optics every generation, which raises content per rack
watch: Datacom revenue growth and gross margin improvement.
